_readme: The one NPC in the game who is not where you left her, met in the running game.
Every leg here ends against a WALL, WATER or a BODY - never a counted number of tiles.
That matters more than usual for this session: the carter is walking while it runs, so
a leg measured in tiles would pass or fail on where she happened to be.
The last leg is the whole point. She patrols column 6 between rows 3 and 8, so walking
NORTH up column 6 must meet her wherever on that route she is - it is geometry that
makes this deterministic, not timing. Then she is talkable like any other NPC, because
movement is behaviour data and her dialog knows nothing about it.

steps.text: the warden opens the game - hear her out first
village: the warden's body stops us north, then east wall, then south onto the town gate
town: down the north road until the south wall stops us
west along the bottom until the well water stops us - that is column 6
north up column 6: her body is the only thing on it, so it is what stops us
and she talks, like any NPC - behaviour is data, her dialog knows nothing of it
the conversation survives 90 frames of her route - the freeze itself is proven in test_world_npcs
